text: Fill in the vitamin or term that completes each sentence about coenzymes and cofactors.
questions: NAD+ and NADP+, which shuttle hydrogen between dehydrogenases, are coenzymes derived from *niacin/nicotinic acid/vitamin B3/B3:Deficiency of this vitamin causes pellagra.*.
FAD, the prosthetic group tightly bound to succinate dehydrogenase, is derived from *riboflavin/vitamin B2/B2:This vitamin's deficiency causes angular stomatitis and glossitis.*.
Thiamine pyrophosphate, the coenzyme of pyruvate dehydrogenase and transketolase, is derived from *thiamine/vitamin B1/B1:Deficiency of this vitamin causes beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy.*.

Pyridoxal phosphate, the coenzyme of transaminases such as ALT and AST, is derived from *pyridoxine/vitamin B6/B6:Lack of this B vitamin in alcoholics lowers ALT activity more than AST, affecting the De Ritis ratio.*.

A co-substrate such as NAD+ binds loosely and leaves after each reaction, whereas a *prosthetic group/prosthetic:What term describes a coenzyme that remains permanently attached to the apoenzyme?* such as FAD is tightly bound and never leaves the enzyme.

overallFeedback.feedback: Most coenzymes are derived from B vitamins: niacin → NAD⁺/NADP⁺, riboflavin → FAD/FMN, thiamine → TPP, pyridoxine → PLP. A co-substrate (like NAD⁺) dissociates after each cycle, while a prosthetic group (like FAD in succinate dehydrogenase) stays bound permanently — the distinction matters because prosthetic groups are recycled in situ on the same enzyme molecule.
